sanskrit: vāsudevād upāttaṃ yad yad astraṃ ca dhanaṃjayāt adarśayata tat kārṣṇiḥ kṛṣṇābhyām aviśeṣayan
english: Whatever weapon the son of Kārṣṇi had received from Vāsudeva and from Dhanaṃjaya, that he displayed, showing himself in no way inferior to the two Kṛṣṇas.

sanskrit: dūram asyan guruṃ bhāraṃ sādhayaṃś ca punaḥ punaḥ saṃdadhad visṛjaṃś ceṣūn nirviśeṣam adṛśyata
english: Shooting far, bearing the heavy burden, and pressing on again and again, nocking and loosing his arrows, he appeared without a single break in his motion.

sanskrit: cāpamaṇḍalam evāsya visphurad dikṣv adṛśyata tamo ghnataḥ sudīptasya savitur maṇḍalaṃ yathā
english: Only the circle of his bow, quivering, was seen in every quarter, like the blazing disk of the sun as it destroys the darkness.

sanskrit: jyāśabdaḥ śuśruve tasya talaśabdaś ca dāruṇaḥ mahāśanimucaḥ kāle payodasyeva nisvanaḥ
english: The twang of his bowstring was heard, and the terrible clap of his palm-guard, like the roar of a storm-cloud loosing its great thunderbolts in season.

sanskrit: hrīmān amarṣī saubhadro mānakṛt priyadarśanaḥ saṃmimānayiṣur vīrān iṣvāsāṃś cāpy ayudhyata
english: Modest yet unforgiving, the son of Subhadrā, proud and fair to look upon, fought on, wishing even to do honor to the heroic archers.

sanskrit: mṛdur bhūtvā mahārāja dāruṇaḥ samapadyata varṣābhyatīto bhagavāñ śaradīva divākaraḥ
english: Having been gentle, O great king, he turned terrible, like the blessed sun grown fierce in autumn after the rains have passed.

sanskrit: śarān vicitrān mahato rukmapuṅkhāñ śilāśitān mumoca śataśaḥ kruddho gabhastīn iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Wrathful, he loosed by the hundred his great and wondrous arrows, gold-feathered and whetted on stone, as the sun pours forth its rays.

sanskrit: kṣuraprair vatsadantaiś ca vipāṭhaiś ca mahāyaśāḥ nārācair ardhanārācair bhallair ajñalikair api
english: With razor-edged shafts and calf-tooth points, with broad-headed and barbed arrows, with iron bolts and half-iron bolts, with crescent heads and finger-broad heads, the illustrious one fought;

sanskrit: avākirad rathānīkaṃ bhāradvājasya paśyataḥ tatas tat sainyam abhavad vimukhaṃ śarapīḍitam
english: he overwhelmed the chariot host before the very eyes of Bhāradvāja, and that army, sore pressed by his arrows, turned its face away.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca dvaidhībhavati me cittaṃ hriyā tuṣṭyā ca saṃjaya mama putrasya yat sainyaṃ saubhadraḥ samavārayat
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: My mind is torn in two, Saṃjaya, between shame and delight, that the son of Subhadrā held back the army of my son.

sanskrit: vistareṇaiva me śaṃsa sarvaṃ gāvalgaṇe punaḥ vikrīḍitaṃ kumārasya skandasyevāsuraiḥ saha
english: Tell me again in full detail, son of Gavalgaṇa, all the sport of that young prince, like Skanda's against the Asuras.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hanta te saṃpravakṣyāmi vimardam atidāruṇam ekasya ca bahūnāṃ ca yathāsīt tumulo raṇaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then I shall recount to you that most fearful struggle, and the tumultuous battle as it raged between the one and the many.

sanskrit: abhimanyuḥ kṛtotsāhaḥ kṛtotsāhān ariṃdamān rathastho rathinaḥ sarvāṃs tāvakān apy aharṣayat
english: Abhimanyu, his ardor kindled, standing upon his chariot, dismayed all your warriors—those eager chariot-fighters and subduers of foes.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ karṇaṃ kṛpaṃ śalyaṃ drauṇiṃ bhojaṃ bṛhadbalam duryodhanaṃ saumadattiṃ śakuniṃ ca mahābalam
english: Droṇa, Karṇa, Kṛpa, Śalya, the son of Droṇa, the Bhoja, Bṛhadbala, Duryodhana, the son of Somadatta, and mighty Śakuni—

sanskrit: nānānṛpān nṛpasutān sainyāni vividhāni ca alātacakravat sarvāṃś caran bāṇaiḥ samabhyayāt
english: the many kings and sons of kings, and the manifold armies—ranging among them all like a whirling firebrand, he assailed them with his arrows.

sanskrit: nighnann amitrān saubhadraḥ paramāstraḥ pratāpavān adarśayata tejasvī dikṣu sarvāsu bhārata
english: Slaying his foes, the son of Subhadrā, master of supreme weapons, glorious and full of splendor, showed himself in every quarter, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā caritaṃ tasya saubhadrasyāmitaujasaḥ samakampanta sainyāni tvadīyāni punaḥ punaḥ
english: Seeing that exploit of the son of Subhadrā of measureless might, your armies trembled again and again.

sanskrit: athābravīn mahāprājño bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān harṣeṇotphullanayanaḥ kṛpam ābhāṣya satvaram
english: Then the deeply wise and valiant Bhāradvāja, his eyes wide with delight, swiftly addressed Kṛpa and said:

sanskrit: ghaṭṭayann iva marmāṇi tava putrasya māriṣa abhimanyuṃ raṇe dṛṣṭvā tadā raṇaviśāradam
english: As though striking at the vital parts of your son, O honored one, when he beheld Abhimanyu, that master of battle, in the fray—

sanskrit: eṣa gacchati saubhadraḥ pārthānām agrato yuvā nandayan suhṛdaḥ sarvān rājānaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhiram
english: "There goes the young son of Subhadrā, at the head of the Pārthas, gladdening all his friends and King Yudhiṣṭhira,

sanskrit: nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca bhīmasenaṃ ca pāṇḍavam bandhūn saṃbandhinaś cānyān madhyasthān suhṛdas tathā
english: and Nakula and Sahadeva and Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava, and his other kinsmen and relations, the neutrals and the well-wishers alike.

sanskrit: nāsya yuddhe samaṃ manye kaṃ cid anyaṃ dhanurdharam icchan hanyād imāṃ senāṃ kimartham api necchati
english: In battle I think no other bowman is his equal; should he wish it, he could slay this whole army—yet for some reason he does not so wish."

sanskrit: droṇasya prītisaṃyuktaṃ śrutvā vākyaṃ tavātmajaḥ ārjuniṃ prati saṃkruddho droṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā smayann iva
english: Hearing these words of Droṇa, spoken with affection, your son grew wrathful against the son of Arjuna, and looking at Droṇa he seemed to smile.

sanskrit: atha duryodhanaḥ karṇam abravīd bāhlikaṃ kṛpam duḥsāsanaṃ madrarājaṃ tāṃs tāṃś cānyān mahārathān
english: Then Duryodhana spoke to Karṇa, to Bāhlika, to Kṛpa, to Duḥśāsana, to the king of the Madras, and to those other great chariot-warriors:

sanskrit: sarvamūrdhāvasiktānām ācāryo brahmavittamaḥ arjunasya sutaṃ mūḍhaṃ nābhihantum ihecchati
english: "The preceptor of all the anointed kings, deepest knower of the Veda, has no wish here to strike down this deluded son of Arjuna.

sanskrit: na hy asya samare mucyed antako 'py ātatāyinaḥ kim aṅga punar evānyo martyaḥ satyaṃ bravīmi vaḥ
english: For in battle not even Death himself, were he the assailant, could escape him—how much less any other mortal? I tell you the truth.

sanskrit: arjunasya sutaṃ tv eṣa śiṣyatvād abhirakṣati putrāḥ śiṣyāś ca dayitās tad apatyaṃ ca dharmiṇām
english: Out of regard for his pupil, he shields the son of Arjuna; for to the righteous, sons and pupils are dear alike, and so too is this their child.

sanskrit: saṃrakṣyamāṇo droṇena manyate vīryam ātmanaḥ ātmasaṃbhāvito mūḍhas taṃ pramathnīta māciram
english: Guarded by Droṇa, he fancies his own prowess; that vain fool, puffed up with self-conceit—crush him without delay!"

sanskrit: evam uktās tu te rājñā sātvatīputram abhyayuḥ saṃrabdhās taṃ jighāṃsanto bhāradvājasya paśyataḥ
english: Thus addressed by the king, they rushed upon the son of the Sātvatī woman, furious and bent on killing him, before the very eyes of Bhāradvāja.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanas tu tac chrutvā duryodhanavacas tadā abravīt kuruśārdūlo duryodhanam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: But Duḥśāsana, that tiger among the Kurus, having heard Duryodhana's words, then said this to Duryodhana:

sanskrit: aham enaṃ haniṣyāmi mahārāja bravīmi te miṣatāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ pāñcālānāṃ ca paśyatām grasiṣyāmy adya saubhadraṃ yathā rāhur divākaram
english: "I shall slay him, great king—I tell you so. Before the watching eyes of the sons of Pāṇḍu and the Pāñcālas, this day I shall devour the son of Subhadrā as Rāhu devours the sun."

sanskrit: utkruśya cābravīd vākyaṃ kururājam idaṃ punaḥ śrutvā kṛṣṇau mayā grastaṃ saubhadram atimāninau gamiṣyataḥ pretalokaṃ jīvalokān na saṃśayaḥ
english: And shouting aloud, he spoke again these words to the king of the Kurus: "When the two over-proud Kṛṣṇas hear that the son of Subhadrā has been devoured by me, they will pass from the world of the living to the world of the dead—of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: tau ca śrutvā mṛtau vyaktaṃ pāṇḍoḥ kṣetrodbhavāḥ sutāḥ ekāhnā sasuhṛdvargāḥ klaibyād dhāsyanti jīvitam
english: "And once those two are clearly dead, the sons sprung from Pāṇḍu's field, together with their company of friends, will in a single day yield up their lives out of despair."

sanskrit: tasmād asmin hate śatrau hatāḥ sarve 'hitās tava śivena dhyāhi mā rājann eṣa hanmi ripuṃ tava
english: "Therefore, when this enemy is slain, all your foes are slain. Bless me, O king, and think on my welfare; here I go to kill your enemy!"

sanskrit: evam uktvā nadan rājan putro duḥśāsanas tava saubhadram abhyayāt kruddhaḥ śaravarṣair avākiran
english: Having spoken thus and roaring, O king, your son Duḥśāsana rushed in fury upon the son of Subhadrā and overwhelmed him with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tam abhikruddham āyāntaṃ tava putram ariṃdamaḥ abhimanyuḥ śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ ṣaḍviṃśatyā samarpayat
english: As your son came on in his wrath, Abhimanyu, that subduer of foes, met him with twenty-six keen arrows.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanas tu saṃkruddhaḥ prabhinna iva kuñjaraḥ ayodhayata saubhadram abhimanyuś ca taṃ raṇe
english: And Duḥśāsana, enraged like an elephant in rut, gave battle to the son of Subhadrā, and Abhimanyu fought him in turn upon the field.

sanskrit: tau maṇḍalāni citrāṇi rathābhyāṃ savyadakṣiṇam caramāṇāv ayudhyetāṃ rathaśikṣāviśāradau
english: Wheeling their chariots leftward and rightward in wondrous circling patterns, the two, skilled in the art of chariot-craft, fought on.

sanskrit: atha paṇavamṛdaṅgadundubhīnāṃ; kṛkaramahānakabherijharjharāṇām ninadam atibhṛśaṃ narāḥ pracakrur; lavaṇajalodbhavasiṃhanādamiśram
english: Then the men raised a mighty din of small drums and tabors and kettledrums, of cymbals and great war-drums and trumpets and rattles, mingled with a roar like that of the briny ocean.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śaravikṣatagātras tu pratyamitram avasthitam abhimanyuḥ smayan dhīmān duḥśāsanam athābravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: His limbs torn by arrows, wise Abhimanyu, smiling, then spoke to Duḥśāsana, who stood before him as his foe:

sanskrit: diṣṭyā paśyāmi saṃgrāme māninaṃ śatrum āgatam niṣṭhuraṃ tyaktadharmāṇam ākrośanaparāyaṇam
english: "By good fortune I behold, come into battle, my arrogant enemy—cruel, having cast off all righteousness, given over to reviling.

sanskrit: yat sabhāyāṃ tvayā rājño dhṛtarāṣṭrasya śṛṇvataḥ kopitaḥ paruṣair vākyair dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ jayonmattena bhīmaś ca bahvabaddhaṃ prabhāṣatā
english: For in the assembly hall, while King Dhṛtarāṣṭra listened, you, drunk with triumph, provoked the Dharma King Yudhiṣṭhira with harsh words, and Bhīma too, prating much that was unseemly.

sanskrit: paravittāpahārasya krodhasyāpraśamasya ca lobhasya jñānanāśasya drohasyātyāhitasya ca
english: For the seizing of another's wealth, for unappeased wrath, for greed, for the ruin of wisdom, for grievous treachery,

sanskrit: pitṝṇāṃ mama rājyasya haraṇasyogradhanvinām tat tvām idam anuprāptaṃ tat kopād vai mahātmanām
english: and for the robbing of the kingdom of my fierce-bowed forefathers—this has now overtaken you, born of the wrath of those great-souled men.

sanskrit: sadyaś cogram adharmasya phalaṃ prāpnuhi durmate śāsitāsmy adya te bāṇaiḥ sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ
english: Reap this very moment the fierce fruit of your unrighteousness, O evil-minded one! Today I shall chastise you with my arrows before the eyes of the whole army.

sanskrit: adyāham anṛṇas tasya kopasya bhavitā raṇe amarṣitāyāḥ kṛṣṇāyāḥ kāṅkṣitasya ca me pituḥ
english: Today in this battle I shall free myself of the debt I owe to that wrath—to the indignant Kṛṣṇā and to the longing of my father.

sanskrit: adya kauravya bhīmasya bhavitāsmy anṛṇo yudhi na hi me mokṣyase jīvan yadi notsṛjase raṇam
english: Today, O Kaurava, I shall discharge in battle my debt to Bhīma. You shall not escape me alive unless you flee the fight."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahābāhur bāṇaṃ duḥśāsanāntakam saṃdadhe paravīraghnaḥ kālāgnyanilavarcasam
english: Having spoken thus, the mighty-armed slayer of hostile heroes nocked an arrow to end Duḥśāsana, gleaming like the fire and wind of doomsday.

sanskrit: tasyoras tūrṇam āsādya jatrudeśe vibhidya tam athainaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā punaś caiva samarpayat
english: Swiftly reaching his breast, it pierced him through at the collarbone; and then once more he met him with twenty-five arrows.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho vyathito rathopastha upāviśat duḥśāsano mahārāja kaśmalaṃ cāviśan mahat
english: Deeply pierced and racked with pain, Duḥśāsana sank down upon the floor of his chariot, O great king, and a great swoon came over him.

sanskrit: sārathis tvaramāṇas tu duḥśāsanam acetasam raṇamadhyād apovāha saubhadraśarapīḍitam
english: His charioteer in haste bore the senseless Duḥśāsana, sore pressed by the arrows of the son of Subhadrā, out of the thick of the battle.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavā draupadeyāś ca virāṭaś ca samīkṣya tam pāñcālāḥ kekayāś caiva siṃhanādam athānadan
english: The Pāṇḍavas and the sons of Draupadī, and Virāṭa, the Pāñcālas and the Kekayas, beholding this, then raised a lion's roar.

sanskrit: vāditrāṇi ca sarvāṇi nānāliṅgāni sarvaśaḥ prāvādayanta saṃhṛṣṭāḥ pāṇḍūnāṃ tatra sainikāḥ
english: And the warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, filled with joy, sounded forth on every side all their instruments of many kinds.

sanskrit: paśyantaḥ smayamānāś ca saubhadrasya viceṣṭitam atyantavairiṇaṃ dṛptaṃ dṛṣṭvā śatruṃ parājitam
english: They watched and smiled at the feat of the son of Subhadrā, seeing their utter and insolent foe defeated.

sanskrit: dharmamārutaśakrāṇām āśvinoḥ pratimās tathā dhārayanto dhvajāgreṣu draupadeyā mahārathāḥ
english: The sons of Draupadī, those great chariot-warriors, bore upon the tips of their standards the images of Dharma, the Wind-god, Śakra, and the two Aśvins.

sanskrit: sātyakiś cekitānaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍinau kekayā dhṛṣṭaketuś ca matsyapāñcālasṛṃjayāḥ
english: Sātyaki and Cekitāna, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, the Kekayas and Dhṛṣṭaketu, the Matsyas, the Pāñcālas, and the Sṛñjayas,

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca mudā yuktā yudhiṣṭhirapurogamāḥ abhyavartanta sahitā droṇānīkaṃ bibhitsavaḥ
english: and the Pāṇḍavas, filled with gladness and led by Yudhiṣṭhira, advanced together, eager to break the host of Droṇa.

sanskrit: tato 'bhavan mahad yuddhaṃ tvadīyānāṃ paraiḥ saha jayam ākāṅkṣamāṇānāṃ śūrāṇām anivartinām
english: Then there arose a mighty battle between your men and their foes, between heroes who longed for victory and would never turn back.

sanskrit: duryodhano mahārāja rādheyam idam abravīt paśya duḥśāsanaṃ vīram abhimanyuvaśaṃ gatam
english: Duryodhana, O great king, said this to the son of Rādhā: "Look at the hero Duḥśāsana, fallen into Abhimanyu's power!

sanskrit: pratapantam ivādityaṃ nighnantaṃ śātravān raṇe saubhadram udyatās trātum abhidhāvanti pāṇḍavāḥ
english: And the Pāṇḍavas come rushing on, roused to rescue him, while the son of Subhadrā, blazing like the sun, strikes down his foes in battle."

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇaḥ śarais tīkṣṇair abhimanyuṃ durāsadam abhyavarṣata saṃkruddhaḥ putrasya hitakṛt tava
english: Then Karṇa, enraged and acting for your son's good, rained keen arrows upon the unassailable Abhimanyu.

sanskrit: tasya cānucarāṃs tīkṣṇair vivyādha parameṣubhiḥ avajñāpūrvakaṃ vīraḥ saubhadrasya raṇājire
english: And on the field of battle that hero, with scorn, pierced with his keen, supreme shafts the followers of the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: abhimanyus tu rādheyaṃ trisaptatyā śilīmukhaiḥ avidhyat tvarito rājan droṇaṃ prepsur mahāmanāḥ
english: But Abhimanyu, high-souled, eager to reach Droṇa, swiftly pierced the son of Rādhā with seventy-three stone-whetted arrows, O king.

sanskrit: taṃ tadā nāśakat kaś cid droṇād vārayituṃ raṇe ārujantaṃ rathaśreṣṭhān vajrahastam ivāsurān
english: None then could hold him back from Droṇa in the battle as he shattered the foremost chariot-warriors, like the Thunderbolt-bearer scattering the Asuras.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo jayaprepsur mānī sarvadhanurbhṛtām saubhadraṃ śataśo 'vidhyad uttamāstrāṇi darśayan
english: Then Karṇa, proudest of all bowmen and longing for victory, pierced the son of Subhadrā a hundredfold, displaying his supreme weapons.

sanskrit: so 'strair astravidāṃ śreṣṭho rāmaśiṣyaḥ pratāpavān samare śatrudurdharṣam abhimanyum apīḍayat
english: With those weapons the valiant pupil of Rāma, foremost of those who know the weapons, harried in battle Abhimanyu, whom foes could not withstand.

sanskrit: sa tathā pīḍyamānas tu rādheyenāstravṛṣṭibhiḥ samare 'marasaṃkāśaḥ saubhadro na vyaṣīdata
english: Yet though thus harried by the son of Rādhā with showers of weapons, the son of Subhadrā, like a god in the battle, did not falter.

sanskrit: tataḥ śilāśitais tīkṣṇair bhallaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ chittvā dhanūṃṣi śūrāṇām ārjuniḥ karṇam ārdayat sa dhvajaṃ kārmukaṃ cāsya chittvā bhūmau nyapātayat
english: Then, with keen, stone-whetted, smooth-jointed broad-headed arrows, the son of Arjuna cut the bows of the heroes and tormented Karṇa; and severing his standard and his bow, he cast them to the ground.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛcchragataṃ karṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇād anantaraḥ saubhadram abhyayāt tūrṇaṃ dṛḍham udyamya kārmukam
english: Then, seeing Karṇa brought to grief, Karṇa's younger brother rushed swiftly upon the son of Subhadrā, raising his stout bow.

sanskrit: tata uccukruśuḥ pārthās teṣāṃ cānucarā janāḥ vāditrāṇi ca saṃjaghnuḥ saubhadraṃ cāpi tuṣṭuvuḥ
english: Then the Pārthas and the men who followed them shouted aloud, and sounded their instruments, and gave praise to the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca so 'bhigarjan dhanuṣpāṇir jyāṃ vikarṣan punaḥ punaḥ tayor mahātmanos tūrṇaṃ rathāntaram avāpatat
english: Saṃjaya said: Roaring aloud, bow in hand, drawing the string again and again, he swiftly closed the gap between the chariots of those two great-souled warriors.

sanskrit: so 'vidhyad daśabhir bāṇair abhimanyuṃ durāsadam sacchatradhvajayantāraṃ sāśvam āśu smayann iva
english: Smiling, as it were, he swiftly pierced the unassailable Abhimanyu with ten arrows, together with his parasol, standard, charioteer, and horses.

sanskrit: pitṛpaitāmahaṃ karma kurvāṇam atimānuṣam dṛṣṭvārditaṃ śaraiḥ kārṣṇiṃ tvadīyā hṛṣitābhavan
english: Seeing the son of Kārṣṇi—who wrought superhuman deeds worthy of his father and forefathers—now wounded by arrows, your men rejoiced.

sanskrit: tasyābhimanyur āyamya smayann ekena patriṇā śiraḥ pracyāvayām āsa sa rathāt prāpatad bhuvi
english: But Abhimanyu, drawing his bow with a smile, struck off that man's head with a single feathered shaft, and he fell from his chariot to the earth.

sanskrit: karṇikāram ivoddhūtaṃ vātena mathitaṃ nagāt bhrātaraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā rājan karṇo vyathāṃ yayau
english: Seeing his brother slain—like a karṇikāra blossom torn by the wind and shaken from the mountain—Karṇa, O king, was struck with grief.

sanskrit: vimukhīkṛtya karṇaṃ tu saubhadraḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ anyān api maheṣvāsāṃs tūrṇam evābhidudruve
english: Having turned Karṇa away with his heron-feathered arrows, the son of Subhadrā at once rushed upon the other great archers as well.

sanskrit: tatas tad vitataṃ jālaṃ hastyaśvarathapattimat jhaṣaḥ kruddha ivābhindad abhimanyur mahāyaśāḥ
english: Then the illustrious Abhimanyu broke through that wide-spread net of elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers, like an angry fish tearing through a snare.

sanskrit: karṇas tu bahubhir bāṇair ardyamāno 'bhimanyunā apāyāj javanair aśvais tato 'nīkam abhidyata
english: And Karṇa, tormented by Abhimanyu's many arrows, withdrew upon his swift horses; thereupon the host was broken open.

sanskrit: śalabhair iva cākāśe dhārābhir iva cāvṛte abhimanyoḥ śarai rājan na prājñāyata kiṃ cana
english: With the sky covered over by Abhimanyu's arrows, as though by locusts or by torrents of rain, O king, nothing could be discerned at all.

sanskrit: tāvakānāṃ tu yodhānāṃ vadhyatāṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ anyatra saindhavād rājan na sma kaś cid atiṣṭhata
english: And as your warriors were being cut down by his sharp arrows, none, O king, save the lord of the Sindhus, stood his ground.
